result.title: Spherical Fixed-Point Reasoners: Adaptive Loop Halting on the Hypersphere
result.summary: Looped (weight-tied) transformers enable adaptive computation by allocating more iterations to harder inputs. Fixed-Point Reasoners (FPRM) achieve this with a damped fixed-point solver, but operate in an unbounded Euclidean residual space with coupled rescaling and relative-norm halting. We introduce Spherical Fixed-Point Reasoners (SFPRM), which perform the same computation on the unit hypersphere of normalized transformers (nGPT). Input injection, damping, and halting become geodesic operations, yielding boundedness by construction and eliminating coefficient coupling. We prove fixed-point existence, local convergence under an explicit step-size condition, and global convergence under strong injection. On Sudoku-Extreme, Maze-Hard, and Mini-ARC, SFPRM achieves 96.6%, 87.9%, and 59.1% test accuracy, respectively, outperforming FPRM and other baselines while allocating test-time compute more effectively. Its converged geometry is also interpretable: token-input angles capture puzzle structure and predict correctness.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Spherical Fixed-Point Reasoners（SFPRM），将权重共享循环 transformer 的阻尼定点求解搬到 nGPT 单位超球面上，使输入注入、阻尼与停机成为测地操作，并在 Sudoku-Extreme、Maze-Hard、Mini-ARC 上报告精度与测试时计算分配。
AI.relevance_reason: 循环迭代、阻尼与自适应停机机制可直接对应 LVR 的 latent 状态生成与 STOP 决策问题；其收敛几何（token-输入夹角编码题型结构并预测正确性）为 latent 状态内容与相似度分析提供了可供核查的线索，但任务为纯文本，向多模态 LVR 迁移仍需验证。
